(2) Type 1 heart attack confirmed by invasive angiography, an ARTEMIS entry criterion (registry): coronary angiography in 63.4% of the lowest income quartile and 64.3% of the highest (same paper); the midpoint 0.6385 is used. 0.7458 x 0.6385 = 0.4762, about 383,000 patients a year

new_source: the share of PMR patients who flare while glucocorticoids are tapered, which is what the indication requires. The European Commission approved Cosentyx on 21 October 2026 for adults with PMR 'who had inadequate response to glucocorticoids or relapse during glucocorticoid taper' (Novartis media release of that date), and REPLENISH (NCT05767034) required 'at least one episode of PMR relapse while attempting to taper prednisone at a dose that is >= 5 mg/day ... within the past 12 weeks'. The paediatric share of US biopsy-confirmed IgAN is 7.4% - 28 of 378 charts were under 18 (DeCongelio M et al., Clin Nephrol 2025;103(1):19-25, doi:10.5414/CN111489, Table 2), the same paper the book's IgAN pool comes from - which would make the overlap 0.926 rather than 1.0, about 14,700 prevalent US children. It is not written as a layer because the eligible share inside it could not be sourced: the trial requires proteinuria at a urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio of 1 g/g or more despite maximum tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB, and no US figure for that share in children exists. The Kidney Health Initiative's own paediatric IgAN literature review (Pediatr Nephrol 2026, doi:10.1007/s00467-026-07245-2) screened 41 epidemiology articles and cites no US paediatric IgAN rate at all. What would settle it: a US paediatric IgAN cohort reporting the proteinuria distribution. The readout is 2030-06-28, so this is not urgent

Maciel G et al., Arthritis Care Res 2017;69:1612-1616 (doi 10.1002/acr.23173, PMC5478481), Olmsted County prevalent cohort on 1 Jan 2015: 9 of 106 with moderate (ESSDAI 5-13) and 7 with high (≥14) systemic activity, so 16/106 = 15.09% meet the ESSDAI ≥5 bar NEPTUNUS-1 and -2 enrolled. This is a floor. The authors warn that retrospective chart scoring under-counts the biological domain. The same group's incident cohort had 29.5% (18/61) at diagnosis (Maciel, Mayo Clin Proc 2017). NEPTUNUS also required diagnosis within 7.5 years and anti-Ro/SSA positivity, which the label may or may not carry. It MUST equal dazodalibep's value exactly: pool_crowding pools only claimants with the same prevalence x eligible_pct.

Capture identity from backend/capture_anchor.py (untreated convention), applied to Saphnelo, the last new biologic mechanism launched into a systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease. Saphnelo US revenue was $8m, $111m, $260m, $425m and $596m in 2021 to 2025 (AZ 20-F 0001104659-24-025553 and 0001104659-26-019130). The net price is $35,856 per patient-year (CMS Part B 2025: $38,007.17 per beneficiary x 1/1.06). That gives treated stocks of 223, 3,096, 7,251, 11,853 and 16,622. After 45.54% stop each year, new starts are 2,974, 5,565, 7,904 and 10,167. Against the untreated CDC SLE pool of 204,295, that is 1.46%, 2.77%, 4.04% and 5.42% (5.04% under the engine pool convention). 2025 is Saphnelo's fourth full year, which is 51.9% of the way up the fitted curve (k 0.31, midpoint 2.76). So the engine needs 10.45% to reproduce 5.42% at the same point. JUDGEMENT: multiple 0.75, giving 0.0784, which converts 4.07% of the untreated eligible pool in ianalumab's fourth year. Case for a higher multiple: it would be the first and only targeted Sjögren's therapy, while Saphnelo launched beside Benlysta. It is a monthly self-injection, not an IV. Two Phase 3s were positive and it has Breakthrough designation. The anchor is measured against all diagnosed SLE patients, not Saphnelo's narrower label pool, so it leans low. Case against: the placebo-adjusted ESSDAI gain was only -1.3 (NEPTUNUS-1, p=0.0496) and -1.0 (NEPTUNUS-2 monthly, p=0.041). The every-3-months arm failed (-0.5, p=0.34), and pooled patient-reported secondaries missed significance. ESSDAI must be scored for payers, and Maciel 2017 found community rheumatologists rarely run those tests. Crowded pool: dazodalibep follows in 2029, and nipocalimab (JNJ), deucravacitinib (BMY), telitacicept (VOR) and efgartigimod (argenx, readout July 2027) all have Sjögren's Phase 3s. None of them carries rows on indication 85 today. Pool crowding: pool_crowding.solve on indication:85 with dazodalibep rations no year (combined starts peak at 11.7% of the eligible pool). Counting the population once trims ianalumab's peak starts to 0.9348 of its standalone run.

new_source: This is the Filspari anchor times 0.5, and the 0.5 is a labelled judgement. I reproduced the capture_anchor identity myself. Filspari US net sales were $29.208mm (2023), $132.222mm (2024) and $322.005mm (2025), from Travere 8-K exhibits 99.1, 0001438533-25-000008 and 0001438533-26-000013. Its CMS Part D 2025 Q1-Q4 figure is $61,544,556.93 over 4,761 claims, or $12,926.81 a 30-tablet claim, which is $157,276.19 a year. That makes stocks of 185.7, 840.7 and 2,047.4 patients. Net of 27.5% stopping each year, new starts are 185.7, 706.1 and 1,437.9. Over the untreated eligible pool (198,887 x 0.6851 = 136,257.5, less prior starts) that is a capture of 0.136%, 0.519% and 1.062% (1.026% on the engine's pool plus incidence). Run through the engine itself (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock, midpoint 1.7, k 1.32), it needs a peak of 0.01617 to reach 2,047.4 patients in year 3. The engine path tracks 219, 828 and 2,047 against the filed 186, 841 and 2,047. That is the 0.0162 povetacicept carries. The 2,047 is a floor, because the stock is divided by a gross price. The multiple of 0.5 gives 0.0081, the same as sefaxersen. Case for going lower: zigakibart is the fourth B-cell entrant. It arrives about 3 years after Voyxact (Nov 2025) and about 2.5 years after Trutakna (Jul 2026) and povetacicept (PDUFA 30 Nov 2026). It doses twice as often as Voyxact and povetacicept. ICER issued an access and affordability alert at $292,500 net: only 6% of eligible patients fit its $821mm budget threshold. Novartis's own Fabhalta and Vanrafia treat the same patients. Case for going higher: Novartis already has a nephrology field force through Fabhalta and Vanrafia, and BEYOND's primary endpoint is eGFR at week 104, which could support full approval where its peers launched on accelerated approval. Cross-check, also a judgement: if the class runs at about 3x Filspari's pace (the povetacicept seed's reading of Voyxact's 90 Q1 2026 beneficiaries) and is split by the order-of-entry penalty of Urban et al., Management Science 1986 (share ratio of about entry order^-0.49), a fourth entrant gets 0.507/2.80 x 3 = 0.54x Filspari, close to the 0.5 chosen. Re-solved 2026-10-05 after untreated patients were given an exit (carryover P/(P+I)): the same target now needs 0.00853856, was 0.0081 (the anchor path, now at carryover 0.9661, solves to 0.0170771, was 0.0161748, times the multiple of 0.5).

Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

new_source: the programme is finished and it failed. NCT03709680, 'Study of Palbociclib Combined With Chemotherapy In Pediatric Patients With Recurrent/Refractory Solid Tumors', Phase 2, Pfizer, completed 2025-08-06 with results posted to the registry. In the randomised Phase 2 part the primary endpoint, investigator-assessed event-free survival, was 1.54 months (95% CI 1.41 to 4.24) with palbociclib added to irinotecan and temozolomide against 4.40 months (95% CI 2.60 to not estimable) without it; blinded independent review read the same way, 1.54 against 4.14. Objective response was 14.3% against 15.8%, median overall survival 10.64 months against 11.43, and grade 3 or 4 adverse events fell on 34 of the palbociclib patients against 17. Adding palbociclib made every endpoint worse. Pfizer's Q1 2026 Pipeline Update (5 May 2026) lists one palbociclib programme, ER+/HER2+ metastatic breast cancer (PATINA) at Registration, and no paediatric solid tumour programme at any phase

new_source: derived: Pfizer generated $23,703mm of free cash flow on $185,759mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 12.76% margin, against the 33.8% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

new_note: amortisation, restructuring and capital spending, none of which the filed lines carry. Read over eight years and not the usual three: Lilly turned 20.0% of revenue into free cash over 2018 to 2022 and 9.4% over 2023 to 2025, the difference being a capacity build-out that took capital spending from 5% of revenue to 12%. Three years takes the trough of that build as the perpetual margin; eight spans both phases
new_source: derived: LLY turned 14.30% of revenue into free cash over 2018 to 2025 against the 38.1% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: LLY paid $3,152mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2018 to 2025, 1.17% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 28.46% to 27.30%. Restated at replacement capex: LLY spent $23,144mm on plant over 2018 to 2025 against $7,255mm of plant depreciation, 5.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 27.30% to 20.25%. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated without working capital build: over 2018 to 2025 LLY's cash flow statement shows receivables up $15,658mm, inventories up $10,223mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $18,257mm, a working capital build of $7,624mm, 2.83% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 20.25% to 16.87%.

WILL-EMI (NCT06998524) enrols patients with confirmed type 3 von Willebrand disease from one month of age in three arms that between them cover the whole treated population: patients previously on intermittent on-demand therapy, randomised against continued on-demand standard of care, and patients previously on prophylaxis one to three times weekly. new_source: a judgement, and the row to argue with. The case for a high share: a subcutaneous injection every one to four weeks against intravenous von Willebrand factor concentrate infused one to three times a week is the same convenience argument that took emicizumab to the majority of US hemophilia A prophylaxis, and this would be the first non-factor prophylactic agent in type 3 disease. The case for a low one, which is why the number is not higher: emicizumab bridges factor IXa and factor X and so substitutes for factor VIII, but it does not replace von Willebrand factor, so it cannot correct the platelet adhesion defect that drives the mucocutaneous, gastrointestinal and menstrual bleeding type 3 patients suffer. Those patients would still need concentrate for that bleeding, which is a reason to prescribe emicizumab alongside rather than instead

none of it. Type 3 von Willebrand disease is a different congenital disorder - absent von Willebrand factor rather than deficient factor VIII - and none of these patients is inside the 4,754mm the asset reports

new_note: a labelled judgement: that patients leave the pool, by lasting remission or death, as fast as they are diagnosed. Without it the engine, which models no exit, grows the pool by 10% of itself every year
new_source: derived to hold the pool at its measured size, as lly_remternetug.csv derives its own: a prevalence of 837,353 with an inflow of 87,749 a year is stationary only if exits equal entries, which sets retention at 837,353 / (837,353 + 87,749) = 0.9051. new_note: the 27 who recurred but needed only a further induction course, and the 13 moved to other therapies, are left out; with them the share would be 96 / 450 = 0.213. new_source: Tome J et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2022;117(8):1311-1315, PMID 35417427 (Olmsted County, MC diagnosed 2002 to 2019; abstract opened 2026-09-28): of 450 patients, 162 were treated with budesonide; 96 recurred after stopping, of whom 56 required long-term budesonide maintenance. 56 / 450 = 0.1244, the budesonide-dependent share, which is the population NCT07156175 enrols: patients on budesonide in remission with a relapse needing budesonide in the prior 8 months

new_note: the 0.25 is the most arguable figure here. For more: it would be the first labelled advanced therapy in MC with nothing else approved beyond budesonide. new_source: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. new_source: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The two reconcile to within a fifth of a point, which is why this is zero rather than absent: the check was run and it found nothing to charge. Restated before interest: ABBV paid $3,002mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2025, 4.91% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. It was held at nil, but ABBV books $7,377mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0001551152-26-000008), 12.06% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -5.94%. Restated without working capital build: over 2025 ABBV's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,490mm, inventories up $234mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $951mm, a working capital build of $773mm, 1.26% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -5.94% to -7.35%.

new_note: the 0.2 multiple is a judgement and the figure the value rests on. The case for more: IMGN151 is designed for low and medium FRalpha tumours (in vivo regressions at H-scores of 30 to 140, AACR 2020 abstract 2890), which Elahere's label, set by MIRASOL at 75% or more of cells staining 2+ or above, leaves out, and AbbVie already sells Elahere to the same prescribers. The case against: no human efficacy has been disclosed since NCT05527184 started in January 2023; the Phase 1b confines its platinum-resistant monotherapy arms to China and Japan and runs its other arms in platinum-sensitive disease, so a US platinum-resistant label is not plainly the route AbbVie is taking, although the Phase 2 readout it names is in platinum-resistant disease; it would arrive about 2033 behind Rina-S (RAINFOL-02, NCT06619236, primary completion 2027-02), R-DXd, AZD5335, sofetabart mipitecan (FRAmework-01, NCT07213804, 2028-11) and mocertatug rezetecan; and AbbVie holds a third FRalpha ADC, ABBV-901, in Phase 1 in ovarian cancer (book asset 1680)
new_source: ANCHOR, the capture_anchor identity on Elahere's US launch. Net price a patient-year = the Part B figure over 1.06: $116,413 in 2025 ($123,397.49) and $114,344 in 2024 ($121,204.42, drug_demand). Stock = revenue over net price: 5,214 in 2025 and 4,712 in 2024. Starts in 2025 = 5,214 - 4,712 x (1 - 0.7724) = 4,142. Over the 12,450 patients a year entering the line (21,010 x 0.5926) that is 33.26%. MULTIPLE 0.2, A JUDGEMENT: 0.2 x 33.26% = 6.65%. It is half the 0.4 the mocertatug rezetecan row takes, the claimant nearest in timing, because mocertatug has a registered Phase 3 (NCT07286266, primary completion 2029-12-17) and published Phase 1 responses, and IMGN151 has neither

new_note: Judgement on which comparator. The engine reads this key (forecast._price_factor), and a biosimilar's defining economics is its price erosion after launch: Mvasi's ASP fell to 30% of Avastin's by 2024 and Kanjinti's to 17% of Herceptin's. Leaving it null would hold the launch price flat for the whole horizon, the most aggressive reading. Mvasi's rate is taken rather than the 29.9% mean of the two, because the engine compounds one constant rate across the horizon and declines slow after year four. Mvasi also held its Medicare volume (12,306 beneficiaries in 2020, 13,212 in 2024), where Kanjinti's fell from 7,550 to 3,365 against four other trastuzumab biosimilars (Horn et al.). The case for faster: Kanjinti's 36.7%, and a crowded first wave of PD-1 biosimilars. The case for slower: Kim et al. (JCO Oncol Pract 2026, doi:10.1200/OP-26-00259) put the bevacizumab biosimilar mean allowed amount at $69.70 (2019) and $33.36 (2023), 16.8% a year on the allowed basis, and Mvasi's own yearly ASP falls were 19.4%, 35.7%, 22.9% and 12.5%, slowing by 2024. The engine freezes the factor at the LOE year it assumes for an unlaunched biologic (launch plus 12, so 2041), where 23.1% compounded prices 2041 at 4.3% of 2029
new_source: drug_demand, CMS Part B spending per dosage unit, converted to ASP as in list_price_per_patient. The biosimilar add-on is 6% of reference ASP to September 2022 and 8% from October 2022 for a qualifying biosimilar (Inflation Reduction Act s.11403; CMS biosimilar FAQs, cms.gov/files/document/biosimilar-faqs.pdf); 2022 is taken at 6.5%. Mvasi ASP $58.42 (2020), $47.11, $30.30, $23.37, $20.45 (2024): 1 - (20.45/58.42)^(1/4) = 23.1% a year. Kanjinti $76.35 (2020) to $12.24 (2024): 36.7% a year

new_note: Judgement on method. The pool is Opdivo's own patients across every indication, so this is measured on them rather than taken from one melanoma trial's median. Under a constant hazard in a steady state, the share of a year's treated patients (beneficiaries) still on drug into the next year equals the patient-years per beneficiary, 0.374, so the engine's stock (S = S x (1-d) + new) is the count of beneficiaries the per-beneficiary price is quoted on. The implied hazard is 1.67 a year, a median time on drug of 5.0 months. eligible_pct is built from this value (new starts = treated patients x 0.6256), so changing one without the other moves the steady-state patient count. The case against: dose holds, weight-based doses and the 1 mg/kg nivolumab induction with ipilimumab lower mg per patient-year and overstate stopping; fixed one-year adjuvant use understates it

new_source: comparator estimate: Novartis's charge as nvs_leqvio.csv carries it, word for word, so growth_investment reads the same restatements off it. derived and found to be nil: NVS's filed expense lines already leave less than the 31.44% of revenue it turned into free cash over 2023 to 2025, so there is nothing left to charge. Restated before interest: NVS paid $2,587mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.72% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 30.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 37.20%, so the charge rebuilds at -7.15%. It was held at nil, but NVS books $3,197mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001114448-26-000004), 5.86% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -5.86%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVS's cash flow statement shows receivables up $3,559mm, inventories up $737mm, payables up $101mm, a working capital build of $4,195mm, 2.79% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -5.86% where the filed figures rebuild it at -7.15%, and stays there. Struck on total revenue: Novartis's filed cost lines sit against net sales of USD 54,532mm and other revenues of USD 2,142mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001114448-26-000004, Note 4), and the income statement shows other revenues above cost of goods sold with no cost of their own, so each ratio is scaled by 54,532 over 56,674 and charged on every revenue the model carries. The book's costs are the filed ones either way; this shares them across the revenue that earned them. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3269 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3911 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -5.8626%.

new_source: Two shares multiplied. (1) Unresectable stage III NSCLC given chemotherapy and radiation as first treatment is 5.369% of all lung cancer diagnoses: of 239,602 lung cancers in SEER over 2000 to 2013, 33,507 were unresectable stage III NSCLC and 12,865 received chemotherapy and radiation (Hansen RN et al., BMC Cancer 2020;20:276, PMC7132866). Over the NSCLC pool that is 5.369% / 0.85 = 6.317%. (2) Concurrent rather than sequential: 35,534 of 42,220 patients given chemoradiation for non-surgically treated stage III NSCLC in the National Cancer Database received it concurrently, 84.2% (Miller ED et al., Radiat Oncol 2018;13:196, PMC6173899: 13,940 of 16,668 elderly and 21,594 of 25,552 younger). new_note: the 0.5 multiple is the most arguable figure here. Durvalumab's own uptake in this setting was immediate: 60.4% of potentially eligible Flatiron patients in the first three months after approval, 66.5% over 18 months (Jairam V et al., J Clin Oncol 2021;39(15_suppl):e20550)
new_source: ANCHOR, measured: 262 of 426 US patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who started concurrent chemoradiation, 61.5%, went on to consolidation durvalumab (Arunachalam A et al., PLoS One 2024;19(11):e0314156, PMC11588217, US Oncology Network, starts 2017 to 2019); death (28.3%) and progression (22.2%) were the main reasons the rest did not. That is Imfinzi's own capture of this pool, the slot oleclumab would share. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 61.5% = 30.75% of each year's patients at peak. For: AstraZeneca owns the backbone and would move its own consolidation patients; in COAST the combination's PFS hazard ratio against durvalumab alone was 0.44 (Barlesi F et al., Future Oncol 2024, doi:10.1080/14796694.2024.2354160); and a rival add-on trial in this setting, PACIFIC-8 with domvanalimab, was discontinued for strategic portfolio prioritisation (appendix of 27 July 2026). Against: the monalizumab arm of the same trial could take the slot instead; a blinded Phase 3 effect is usually smaller than an open-label Phase 2 one; the combination adds infusions in the first two cycles; and Tagrisso's US label now covers EGFR-mutant unresectable stage III disease after chemoradiation (DailyMed, in the book's labels table), which takes those patients out of durvalumab consolidation after the 2017 to 2019 measurement

Cross-check on the same basis: 79.3% of first-line mCRPC patients came from mHSPC (Hooper 2026), so 0.115 x 0.793 = 9.11% of diagnoses reach mCRPC from mHSPC, 71% of the 12.81% entering it, which leaves room for deaths before castration resistance. Devasia back-calculates from 2000 to 2017 SEER data and distant-stage incidence rose 5.3% a year in men 45 to 74 and 6.5% in men 75 and over to 2018 (Desai et al., JAMA Netw Open 2022, jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2790041), so the pool leans low. The case for a smaller pool: AMPLITUDE enrolled every protocol-defined HRR alteration, 56% of them BRCA1 or BRCA2, yet FDA approved Akeega only 'for the treatment of patients with BRCA2-mutated metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer' (Johnson & Johnson press release, 2025-12-12), so a saruparib label narrower than the HRRm cohort is a live risk
new_source: Two shares multiplied. First, 12.81% of diagnoses enter metastatic castration-sensitive disease each year. 6.8% of US cases are metastatic at diagnosis and de novo cases are 45% of the men living with metastatic prostate cancer (Devasia et al., Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2023;32(5):659-65, doi:10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-22-1038, PMC10159917; its base case gives de novo and recurrent disease the same survival, so the incidence split is the prevalence split): 0.068 / 0.45 = 15.11% of diagnoses become metastatic. Less the men whose first metastases are already castration-resistant: 1,019 of 5,096 US patients starting first-line mCRPC therapy (20.0%) came from non-metastatic CRPC (Flatiron; Hooper et al., JAMA Netw Open 2026;9(6):e2620750, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20750), on the book's 11.5% mCRPC share: 0.1511 - 0.115 x 0.200 = 12.81%, about 40,200 men a year. Second, 17.86% carry a protocol-defined HRR alteration: 1,054 of 5,903 men with mCSPC prescreened for AMPLITUDE with a valid result (Attard et al., Nat Med 2025, doi:10.1038/s41591-025-03961-8). 0.1281 x 0.1786 = 0.02288, about 7,180 men a year

new_note: analogue, the most arguable figure here. The ratio does not depend on the Spanish positivity rate: Adelphi's own pooled figures, HRR alterations known in 13% of mCSPC and 18% of mCRPC patients, give (0.13 / 0.1786) x (0.07 / 0.18) = 0.283, and its 38% positivity among the men tested says testing is selective, which a ratio of the two settings absorbs. The case for more: HRR gene testing in metastatic prostate cancer rose 17 points, 26% to 43%, between the 2020 and 2022-2023 waves of the same programme and AMPLITUDE supports testing as routine in mCSPC; saruparib is PARP1-selective, where 25% of AMPLITUDE's niraparib arm needed a transfusion. The case for less: this gives saruparib the whole PARP class, and FDA approved Akeega (niraparib with abiraterone) in BRCA2-mutated mCSPC on 2025-12-12 (Johnson & Johnson press release), so saruparib would launch as the second PARP option in the setting; Akeega reached 93 Medicare Part D beneficiaries in 2025 (CMS file 4ff7c618); and in first-line mCRPC, where the PARP and ARPI combinations are labelled, PARP-based regimens stayed under 2.5% of starts across 2021 to 2025 (Hooper 2026)
new_source: Decomposed into who is found and who is treated once found, on US rates because the model and the treatment share are US. Found: 39% of US men with mCSPC had HRR genes tested in the 2022-2023 wave of the Adelphi Real World Prostate Cancer Disease Specific Programme (Future Oncol 2025, doi:10.1080/14796694.2025.2577337, PMC12622337: HRR gene testing rates 'were highest in the United States (mCSPC: 27% and 39%; mCRPC: 37% and 53%)' in the 2020 and 2022-2023 waves; the 34% and 47% the paper reports overall pool France, Germany and the US). Treated once found: in the 2024 US Flatiron cohort PARP-based regimens were 24 of 344 second-line mCRPC starts, 7.0% (Hooper et al. 2026), against 53% of US mCRPC patients tested for HRR genes (Adelphi, same wave) and 18% of tested mCRPC patients carrying an alteration (1,412 centrally tested mCRPC samples, Cancers 2026;18(10):1614, doi:10.3390/cancers18101614), so PARP starts in that line equal 0.07 / (0.53 x 0.18) = 73.4% of the men known to carry one. 0.39 x 0.734 = 0.286 of each year's HRRm mCSPC men, about 2,050 starts a year at peak. No verifiable independent forecast covers the prostate indication: GlobalData's analyst consensus of $628mm of global sales in 2030 (Clinical Trials Arena, GlobalData Healthcare comment, 2025-06-04, clinicaltrialsarena.com/analyst-comment/asco-2025-akeega-parp-therapy-mcspc/) and a US figure from its expiry model ($340mm in 2036, seen only in a search summary of a page that could not be opened) both span every indication, so neither is solved to

new_source: comparator estimate: Vertex's charge as vrtx_zimislecel.csv carries it, word for word, so growth_investment reads the same restatements off it. derived: Vertex generated $12,074mm of free cash flow on $49,396mm of revenue over the five years to 2025, a 24.44% margin, against the 33.0% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Five years rather than three because operating cash flow was negative $493mm in 2024 on the Alpine acquisition, which takes a three-year window to 17.5% and lets one deal set the rate. Solved so the modelled book reproduces the margin rather than taken off a single line. Restated before interest: VRTX paid $195mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2021 to 2025, 0.39% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 10.33% to 9.94%. Restated at replacement capex: VRTX spent $1,375mm on plant over 2021 to 2025 against $758mm of plant depreciation, 1.25% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 9.94% to 8.47%. Restated without one-off cash: VRTX's free cash flow over 2021 to 2025 carried $6,517mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately. None recurs, so the charge falls from 8.47% to 0.00%. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 39.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2021 to 2025 supports 43.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.72%. new_note: JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 1.0 on the second-line LBCL share, read as a lifetime share. The second line matches the trial's failure of one prior immunomodulator. The incumbent is CAR T itself, in its only measured setting: referral from community physicians to certified centres, apheresis and lymphodepletion, the same barriers a rheumatology patient meets. No US count of autologous transplants for SSc (the one-time cellular incumbent in this disease) was found. At the third-line 35.7%, p would be 0.0328. Case for lower: the 25% is shared by several CAR Ts, and zola-cel will meet rese-cel (Cabaletta), rapcabtagene autoleucel (Novartis) and bispecific T-cell engagers in SSc. Refractory SSc-ILD is not fatal within months as relapsed LBCL is, and it has chronic alternatives (tocilizumab, rituximab, nintedanib). The LBCL denominator is fit patients only, while this pool is not filtered for fitness. The class-wide autoimmune CAR T pause of September 2026 (IEC-HS after three deaths on Novartis's product) may make referrers cautious. Case for higher: patients are younger, a drug-free remission after one infusion appeals, a refractory patient faces repeated escalation decisions over years, and FDA's removal of the CAR T REMS eases logistics. Modelled peak is about 38 patients a year, US plus ex-US
new_source: Perales MA et al., 'Real-world treatment patterns of patients with large B-cell lymphoma over time and into a post-CAR T approval era', Blood Adv 2026;10(15):5325-5337, doi:10.1182/bloodadvances.2025019064 (PMID 42234934; Flatiron, mostly community practices): 32 of 128 (25.0%) clearly fit patients eligible for second-line CAR T received it in 2022 to April 2024; 65 of 182 (35.7%) fit third-line patients received it in 2018-2021. Solved through the engine's identity so that a patient in the eligible pool has a 25% chance of being treated before leaving it: p / (1 - (1 - p) x 0.938931) = 0.25, so p = 0.25 x (1 - 0.938931) / (1 - 0.25 x 0.938931) = 0.01995

Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. new_source: comparator estimate: Merck's charge as mrk_calderasib.csv carries it, word for word, so growth_investment reads the same restatements off it. derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.

new_source: two shares multiplied. (1) 53% go on to a second line: Coleman et al., J Health Econ Outcomes Res 2023 (doi:10.36469/001c.87853), of 1,961 US patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer who started a first line, 53% started a second, the share mrk_sacituzumab_tirumotecan.csv and gsk_mocertatug_rezetecan.csv take. (2) 51.2% HER2-expressing: van Dijk D et al., J Clin Oncol 2025;43(4):443-452, 806 endometrial cancers across histotypes and molecular classes, found 35.6% HER2-low (IHC 1+, or 2+ without amplification) and 15.6% HER2-positive in recurrent or metastatic disease, 51.2% in all. 0.53 x 0.512 = 0.27136, about 7,060 patients a year

In advanced GIST (MetaGIST) KIT mutations are found in 82.8% and PDGFRA in 2.1% (Emile JF et al., Med Oncol 2012;29(3):1765-72, doi:10.1007/s12032-011-0074-y, PMID 21953054). 0.5021 x 0.828 = 0.4157

The case for lower: StrateGIST 3 compares against sunitinib alone, not the combination that will be standard by readout, so velzatinib may launch without a head-to-head answer to it; Hsu's denominator excludes patients who received neither option, so the share overstates capture of this pool; the setting is Taiwan, not the US. new_source: Two parts. (1) Sunitinib's measured second-line share: Hsu JT et al., Oncotarget 2017;8(41):71128-37, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.16795, PMID 29050348 (Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, July 2004 to December 2010): of 521 advanced GIST patients failing first-line imatinib 400 mg and treated with dose escalation or sunitinib, 125 escalated then switched to sunitinib and 150 switched directly, so 275 (52.78%) received sunitinib after imatinib. (2) An order-of-entry cut, because velzatinib will not be the first branded drug to beat sunitinib in second line: Cogent's bezuclastinib plus sunitinib beat sunitinib in the PEAK Phase 3 (median PFS 16.5 against 9.2 months, HR 0.50, Cogent 8-K 10 November 2025) and its NDA was accepted with priority review and a PDUFA date of 2026-11-30 (Cogent release, 28 May 2026), more than three years before velzatinib's 2030 start. new_note: a four-fold published range, and the low end is taken deliberately rather than the midpoint. new_note: the case for lower: two generic antipsychotics already hold this indication, paediatric antipsychotic prescribing is conservative, and no long-term paediatric safety read-out exists before NCT06229210 completes in 2032. The case for higher: metabolic burden is the reason families stop risperidone and aripiprazole, and a tolerability-led branded entrant in paediatric psychiatry has taken more than a tenth of a generic market before. Settled by years of sales, not by an event

derived: JNJ's free cash conversion against what its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: JNJ paid $5,540mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 2.07% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 2.11% to 0.04%. Restated at replacement capex: JNJ spent $13,799mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $8,728mm of depreciation and amortisation less amortisation of intangibles, 1.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 0.04% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: JNJ's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $6,000mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,500mm; 2024 instalment 2,000mm; 2025 instalment 2,500mm). None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 27.17% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 31.91%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.74%. It was held at nil, but JNJ books $4,600mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000200406-26-000016), 4.88% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -4.74%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 JNJ's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,811mm, inventories up $3,901mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $6,344mm, a working capital build of $368mm, 0.14% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -4.74% to -4.88%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.2766 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3207 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -4.4065%.

HLD-0915 is an oral once-daily androgen receptor-directed medicine built to work after ARPI resistance, so the place it is designed to take is the second ARPI, and 29.7% is the most any one medicine holds of this line. new_source: already approved. RYBREVANT (openFDA drug/label set 1466c070-9f97-4fa4-a955-6a6b59981fb8, effective 2025-11-11) is indicated in locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R mutations, first line with lazertinib and after an EGFR TKI with carboplatin and pemetrexed, and in exon 20 insertion disease first line with carboplatin and pemetrexed and as a single agent after platinum-based chemotherapy. RYBREVANT FASPRO, the subcutaneous form (set 9e58b045-e352-4f62-99bf-77fae1bebc69, effective 2026-06-17), carries the same four indications, and LAZCLUZE (set c417f9ee-2027-4ed5-92ad-3c19266de16c) the first-line one. COCOON (NCT06120140, Phase 2, 305 enrolled, primary completion 2027-05-31) enrols treatment-naive exon 19 deletion or L858R disease treated first line with amivantamab and lazertinib and randomises the dermatologic management, prophylactic antibiotics and skin care against standard care; its primary endpoint is grade 2 or worse skin adverse events at 12 weeks. PALOMA-2 (NCT05498428, Phase 2, 520 planned, primary completion 2027-08-17) gives subcutaneous amivantamab in eight cohorts, every one an EGFR-mutated NSCLC setting the label covers: first line with lazertinib (cohorts 1, 5, 6), exon 20 first line with chemotherapy (2), after osimertinib with chemotherapy with or without lazertinib (3, 3b), after amivantamab and lazertinib with chemotherapy (7), and a switch from intravenous to subcutaneous dosing (4)

0.610 x 0.53 x 0.60 = 0.19398, a label pool of 4,153,888 of 21,414,000. First, 61.0% of adults with a past-year major depressive episode received treatment (NIMH, NSDUH 2021). This is any treatment, including counselling alone, so it overstates the share on an SSRI or SNRI; the label will require one. Second, 53% respond inadequately to the first SSRI: STAR*D level 1 citalopram response was 47% (Trivedi MH et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:28-40, doi 10.1176/appi.ajp.163.1.28). Third, about 60% of MDD patients have clinically relevant insomnia symptoms despite an SSRI or SNRI. That figure is J&J's own, from its press release of 2026-05-11, not an independent study. This 19.4% of MDD is the adjunctive-with-insomnia share the audit asked for.

new_source: Auvelity's measured capture, using the identity in capture_anchor.py (untreated pool, no opening stock) on Axsome's filed Auvelity net revenue: $130.1mm in 2023, $291.4mm in 2024, $507.1mm in 2025. Net price per beneficiary is $2,730.57 (its 2025 Part D $5,461.14, halved), and the pool is its whole label, 21,414,000. Stock: 47,646, 106,718 and 185,712. Carried forward at 9% (discontinuation 0.91): 0, 4,288 and 9,605. New starts: 47,646, 102,430 and 176,108. Capture rates: 0.2225%, 0.4794% and 0.8282% (2025, over an untreated pool of 21,263,925). The 2025 rate is the anchor because it is the last full year with a single label. The Q2 2026 run-rate ($180.3mm times 4) gives 1.1732%, but Auvelity added Alzheimer's agitation in June 2026. The anchor at the alternative discontinuation of 0.70 is 0.7225%. MULTIPLE 0.75x, A JUDGEMENT: 0.8282% x 0.75 = 0.6212% of seltorexant's own untreated label pool. For a higher multiple: the label pool is narrow and every patient in it is actively changing therapy; J&J has psychiatry sales scale; residual insomnia is common, and against quetiapine XR seltorexant showed four times less somnolence and less weight gain. Against: only one of two placebo-controlled Phase 3s was positive (a 2.6-point MADRS gain); it was not significantly better than generic quetiapine XR; and it enters a crowded add-on class of Rexulti, Vraylar, generic aripiprazole and quetiapine, and J&J's own Caplyta. Caplyta took the adjunctive MDD label on 2025-11-06 with 4.9 and 4.5 points against placebo, so J&J may put Caplyta first. At 1.0x the peak is 0.8282%.

new_source: Anchor: Elahere's 2025 US starts of 4,142 = 0.3327 of the all-comers PROC cohort of 12,450. The derivation is on GSK's ovarian row: - US revenue: $607mm (2025), $538.8mm (2024, annualised). - Net price: $116,413 per patient-year. - Stock: 5,214 (2025) against 4,712 (2024), with 77.24% stopping. - In 2026 the rate is 0.3490 (Q2 x 4). Peak = 0.3327 x multiple 0.5 = 0.1663. The multiple is a JUDGEMENT. Case for a higher multiple: - Breakthrough designation (20 Jan 2026) after bevacizumab and mirvetuximab. - Activity at every FRalpha level: ORR 40% at 0-24% expression and 54% at 75% or more. - ORR 50% in 104 patients. - An all-comers label about 2.8 times Elahere's FRalpha-high label, and a head-to-head arm against chemotherapy or mirvetuximab. Case against: - Arrives about 2030 into a crowded class. - Genmab's Rina-S is also an FRalpha ADC for all comers and reads out about two years earlier (NCT06619236, 2027-02). - R-DXd PROC (2028-02, Breakthrough) and AZD5335 (2028-11) come first too. - FRAmework-01 excludes patients who had a prior topoisomerase-payload ADC. - Elahere is modelled off its own revenue, so share taken from it is counted twice. The multiple is set above GSK's 0.4 because Sofe-M reaches PROC about two years earlier and holds Breakthrough. Carryover: at 0, this drug's US revenue at year 10 is about $311mm; at the book default of 1.0 it is about $1.8bn, because the curve then converges on the whole cohort.

new_source: ANCHOR, a measured analogue: the PCSK9 inhibitors, the last high-priced injectable lipid class to launch into a prevalent US pool against payer prior authorisation. That is the engine's penetration itself, new starts over eligible patients, so it is fitted directly: a logistic with peak 0.0142, k 3.06 and midpoint -0.55 years from the first full year (2016) fits the five years to an rmse of 0.17 points, 2015 taken at year -1 as measured and not annualised. MULTIPLE 0.25, A JUDGEMENT: 0.25 x 0.0142 = 0.00355. The case: that rate was a whole class with two drugs; solbinsiran would be the third RNA drug into sHTG after olezarsen (approved June 2026) and plozasiran, both APOC3, which cut triglycerides by about 80% in sHTG (SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 medians of 79% and 81%, Arrowhead 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-06-30) against solbinsiran's 58% to 60% in mixed dyslipidaemia (NCT05256654), and olezarsen and plozasiran report fewer pancreatitis events where solbinsiran has no such data. For it: ANGPTL3 silencing also lowered apoB in PROLONG-ANG3 (24.3% at 400 mg against 11.6% on placebo at day 180), a second lipid benefit

new_source: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. The window barely matters here, unlike Pfizer: the same aggregate is 21.9% over five years and 21.3% over every year on file. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.

new_source: the share of PMR patients who flare while glucocorticoids are tapered, which is what the indication requires. Benlysta (belimumab) CMS Medicare Part D 2025, from the quarterly companion 4ff7c618 (Q1-Q4 2025): $291,468,828 over 7,431 beneficiaries = $39,223.37 per beneficiary. Why this comparator: no systemic Sjögren's therapy is marketed in the US, and Novartis itself calls ianalumab the potential first targeted treatment. Benlysta is the closest marketed match. It acts on the same BAFF pathway (it targets the ligand, ianalumab the receptor). It is prescribed by rheumatologists for SLE, the neighbouring systemic autoimmune disease. Its subcutaneous form is self-injected on the pharmacy benefit, as monthly 300 mg subcutaneous ianalumab will be (NCT06293365 tests its 2 mL autoinjector). The 2024 annual Part D figure was $37,182. Alternative: Benlysta Part B at $36,043.10 per beneficiary with a 0.056604 discount gives a net of $34,003, 73% above this net. Benlysta's mature per-beneficiary figure is used as is, not annualised.

Maciel G et al., Arthritis Care Res 2017;69:1612-1616 (doi 10.1002/acr.23173, PMC5478481), Olmsted County prevalent cohort on 1 Jan 2015: 9 of 106 with moderate (ESSDAI 5-13) and 7 with high (≥14) systemic activity, so 16/106 = 15.09% meet the ESSDAI ≥5 bar NEPTUNUS-1 and -2 enrolled. This is a floor. The authors warn that retrospective chart scoring under-counts the biological domain. The same group's incident cohort had 29.5% (18/61) at diagnosis (Maciel, Mayo Clin Proc 2017). NEPTUNUS also required diagnosis within 7.5 years and anti-Ro/SSA positivity, which the label may or may not carry. It MUST equal dazodalibep's value exactly: pool_crowding pools only claimants with the same prevalence x eligible_pct.

Capture identity from backend/capture_anchor.py (untreated convention), applied to Saphnelo, the last new biologic mechanism launched into a systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease. Saphnelo US revenue was $8m, $111m, $260m, $425m and $596m in 2021 to 2025 (AZ 20-F 0001104659-24-025553 and 0001104659-26-019130). The net price is $35,856 per patient-year (CMS Part B 2025: $38,007.17 per beneficiary x 1/1.06). That gives treated stocks of 223, 3,096, 7,251, 11,853 and 16,622. After 45.54% stop each year, new starts are 2,974, 5,565, 7,904 and 10,167. Against the untreated CDC SLE pool of 204,295, that is 1.46%, 2.77%, 4.04% and 5.42% (5.04% under the engine pool convention). 2025 is Saphnelo's fourth full year, which is 51.9% of the way up the fitted curve (k 0.31, midpoint 2.76). So the engine needs 10.45% to reproduce 5.42% at the same point. JUDGEMENT: multiple 0.75, giving 0.0784, which converts 4.07% of the untreated eligible pool in ianalumab's fourth year. Case for a higher multiple: it would be the first and only targeted Sjögren's therapy, while Saphnelo launched beside Benlysta. It is a monthly self-injection, not an IV. Two Phase 3s were positive and it has Breakthrough designation. The anchor is measured against all diagnosed SLE patients, not Saphnelo's narrower label pool, so it leans low. Case against: the placebo-adjusted ESSDAI gain was only -1.3 (NEPTUNUS-1, p=0.0496) and -1.0 (NEPTUNUS-2 monthly, p=0.041). The every-3-months arm failed (-0.5, p=0.34), and pooled patient-reported secondaries missed significance. ESSDAI must be scored for payers, and Maciel 2017 found community rheumatologists rarely run those tests. Crowded pool: dazodalibep follows in 2029, and nipocalimab (JNJ), deucravacitinib (BMY), telitacicept (VOR) and efgartigimod (argenx, readout July 2027) all have Sjögren's Phase 3s. None of them carries rows on indication 85 today. Pool crowding: pool_crowding.solve on indication:85 with dazodalibep rations no year (combined starts peak at 11.7% of the eligible pool). Counting the population once trims ianalumab's peak starts to 0.9348 of its standalone run.

new_source: ANCHOR, the capture_anchor identity applied to Multaq on this row's pool, with the engine's convention that a year's starts come from the untreated pool plus that year's eligible diagnoses. US revenue from Sanofi's 20-F product tables: EUR278mm in 2024 (0001121404-25-000010) and EUR285mm in 2025 (0001628280-26-008403), at the FRED DEXUSEU annual averages of 1.0820 (251 daily rates) and 1.1306 (250): $300.8mm and $322.2mm. Net per patient = 0.5 x the Part D figure a beneficiary above ($5,700.19 in 2024, $6,083.17 in 2025): $2,850.09 and $3,041.58. Stock: 105,539 and 105,939. At this file's 50.30% stopping, 49.70% remain, so 2025 new starts are 105,939 - 105,539 x 0.4970 = 53,487. The pool is 10,550,000 x 0.70 = 7,385,000 eligible, less the 105,539 on Multaq, plus 700,000 eligible diagnoses (1,000,000 x 0.70) = 7,979,461. Capture: 53,487 / 7,979,461 = 0.670%, which is the anchor (0.735% without the year's diagnoses). CROSS-CHECK: the revenue basis counts 1.46 Multaq patients per 2025 Part D beneficiary (105,939 against 72,363), plausible for a drug of older patients; and 2,977 of 143,281 newly diagnosed adults (2.1%) started dronedarone within 90 days (Kipp et al. 2024). MULTIPLE 1.0, A JUDGEMENT: parity with Multaq, 1.0 x 0.670% = 0.67%. For more: a first-in-class mechanism in a class of old drugs, and Novartis already sells Entresto and Leqvio to cardiologists. Against: the evidence is a 165-patient Phase 2 on a surrogate endpoint that has not read out; generic antiarrhythmics took 91% of first starts against dronedarone's 8% (Tardos et al. 2021); and 9.5% of antiarrhythmic starters had a catheter ablation within two years (Kipp et al. 2024), the non-drug route to the same rhythm control

Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVS's cash flow statement shows receivables up $3,559mm, inventories up $737mm, payables up $101mm, a working capital build of $4,195mm, 2.79% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -5.86% where the filed figures rebuild it at -7.15%, and stays there. The registry's 2028-04-14 date is the end of the open-label extension and substudy, whose primary outcomes are adverse event counts

new_source: JUDGEMENT. NCT07094516 completes 2028-09-14 (ClinicalTrials.gov, updated 2026-06-26), no Phase 3 is registered, and Novartis gives first submission as 2029 or later (FY2025 20-F, Q2 2026 6-K). Novartis's own gap from a Phase 2b completion to a Phase 3 start is remibrutinib's 10.5 months (NCT03926611 completed 2021-01-14, NCT05030311 started 2021-11-30), so a Phase 3 starts about July 2029. Kisunla went from its Phase 3 start (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2, NCT04437511, 2020-06-19) to its first full year, 2025, in 4.53 years, and Leqembi from Clarity AD (NCT03887455, 2019-03-27) to 2024 in 4.77 years (the intervals mrk_mk_2214.csv records). July 2029 plus 4.5 to 4.8 years reaches February to May 2034, so the first full year on sale is 2035

new_source: a scaling to a sourced absolute label pool, the one trontinemab, BMS-986446 and MK-2214 carry: about 2.2 million US residents could be eligible for lecanemab, amyloid-positive with MCI or mild dementia (Dittrich A et al., Neurology 2024;102(9):e209402), over the 7,400,000 aged 65 and over with Alzheimer's dementia that data/epidemiology.csv carries. 2.2 / 7.4 = 0.297

new_note: the 0.5 is the most arguable figure here. For more: a new mechanism acting on microglia rather than on amyloid or tau, with a clinical primary endpoint in its Phase 2, and TREM2 is better validated in Alzheimer's than ALS (Guggenheim, reported by European Biotechnology). Against: the first TREM2 agonist antibody, Alector's AL002, 'failed to meet the primary endpoint' of CDR-SB in INVOKE-2 (Alector release, 2024-11-25); VHB937 itself missed both endpoints in ALS; it is a further infusion beside anti-amyloid therapy; and it would launch about 2035 behind subcutaneous and brain-shuttle antibodies
new_source: ANCHOR, the measured anti-amyloid class new-start rate from CMS Part B beneficiaries, queried 2026-09-28. Leqembi (J0174): 961 in 2023 and 7,907 in 2024 (Medicare Part B Spending by Drug, dataset 76a714ad-3a2c-43ac-b76d-9dadf8f7d890) and 14,029 in 2025 (quarterly file bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)'). Kisunla (J0175): 1,299 in 2024 (drug_demand) and 9,993 in 2025 (quarterly file). At this seed's stopping of 0.724702, 27.53% of a year's patients carry into the next, so 2025 new starts are 14,029 - 7,907 x 0.2753 = 11,852 and 9,993 - 1,299 x 0.2753 = 9,635, 21,488 together. A year's eligible pool in the engine's terms is the carried pool plus the inflow, in the first year 2,197,800 + 270,270 = 2,468,070, so the class started 0.8706% of it in 2025. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 0.8706% = 0.4353%, the multiple MK-2214 and BMS-986446 take
new_unit: share of the eligible untreated pool started per year

It is self-injected every 4 weeks (openFDA label, effective 2026-03-17: 400 mg once every 4 weeks, one single-dose syringe per carton), so it matches zigakibart on class, disease and care setting. The source is CMS Medicare Quarterly Part D Spending by Drug (dataset 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), 2026 Q1, still the latest quarter carrying Voyxact: $4,640,340.95 over 151 claims is $30,730.73 a claim, and 13 four-week doses a year gives $399,499.49. It is the same class price povetacicept carries, and sefaxersen carries it converted to CHF. Alternatives: the published WAC of about $390,000 a year (ICER, B-Cell Directed Therapies for IgAN, 2026), which the per-claim figure sits 2.4% above; Trutakna (atacicept) at about $425,000 per the povetacicept seed (not re-verified here); Fabhalta at a 2026 Q1 Part D $47,568.79 a claim (monthly fill), about $570,800 a year, as the upside case. new_source: This is the Filspari anchor times 0.5, and the 0.5 is a labelled judgement. I reproduced the capture_anchor identity myself. Filspari US net sales were $29.208mm (2023), $132.222mm (2024) and $322.005mm (2025), from Travere 8-K exhibits 99.1, 0001438533-25-000008 and 0001438533-26-000013. Its CMS Part D 2025 Q1-Q4 figure is $61,544,556.93 over 4,761 claims, or $12,926.81 a 30-tablet claim, which is $157,276.19 a year. That makes stocks of 185.7, 840.7 and 2,047.4 patients. Net of 27.5% stopping each year, new starts are 185.7, 706.1 and 1,437.9. Over the untreated eligible pool (198,887 x 0.6851 = 136,257.5, less prior starts) that is a capture of 0.136%, 0.519% and 1.062% (1.026% on the engine's pool plus incidence). Run through the engine itself (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock, midpoint 1.7, k 1.32), it needs a peak of 0.01617 to reach 2,047.4 patients in year 3. The engine path tracks 219, 828 and 2,047 against the filed 186, 841 and 2,047. That is the 0.0162 povetacicept carries. The 2,047 is a floor, because the stock is divided by a gross price. The multiple of 0.5 gives 0.0081, the same as sefaxersen. Case for going lower: zigakibart is the fourth B-cell entrant. It arrives about 3 years after Voyxact (Nov 2025) and about 2.5 years after Trutakna (Jul 2026) and povetacicept (PDUFA 30 Nov 2026). It doses twice as often as Voyxact and povetacicept. ICER issued an access and affordability alert at $292,500 net: only 6% of eligible patients fit its $821mm budget threshold. Novartis's own Fabhalta and Vanrafia treat the same patients. Case for going higher: Novartis already has a nephrology field force through Fabhalta and Vanrafia, and BEYOND's primary endpoint is eGFR at week 104, which could support full approval where its peers launched on accelerated approval. Cross-check, also a judgement: if the class runs at about 3x Filspari's pace (the povetacicept seed's reading of Voyxact's 90 Q1 2026 beneficiaries) and is split by the order-of-entry penalty of Urban et al., Management Science 1986 (share ratio of about entry order^-0.49), a fourth entrant gets 0.507/2.80 x 3 = 0.54x Filspari, close to the 0.5 chosen. Re-solved 2026-10-05 after untreated patients were given an exit (carryover P/(P+I)): the same target now needs 0.00853856, was 0.0081 (the anchor path, now at carryover 0.9661, solves to 0.0170771, was 0.0161748, times the multiple of 0.5).

new_source: This is the book's own fit to Tarpeyo, the first IgAN-specific launch, carried so that all three IgAN claimants share one curve. The book fits k 1.32, midpoint 1.70, rmse 17. My independent least-squares refit gives k 1.36, midpoint 1.67, rmse 16.5, the same shape on a flat error surface. Filspari (112, 323, 660 over 2023 to 2025) fits k 1.30, midpoint 1.66, but three points for three parameters is exact, so it describes the curve rather than testing it. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

new_note: House convention: Padcev is the closest marketed comparator, an MMAE ADC that with pembrolizumab is the first-line la/mUC standard DV+P would compete against. The Part D channel carries 112 Padcev beneficiaries in 2025 ($12,635,630.43, quarterly companion 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), 1.7% of spend; it is left out because it prices on the Part D convention, and summing both parts would give $107,937. 57,101 Part B claims over 6,773 beneficiaries is 8.4 administrations each. Not annualised, by the book's rule: the per-beneficiary basis is the one measured against negotiated prices. Alternative: Enhertu, the marketed HER2 ADC, at $72,455.15 a Part B beneficiary in the same 2025 file. No price for DV exists, since it is not approved in the US
new_source: Padcev (enfortumab vedotin, HCPCS J9177), CMS Medicare Part B quarterly file, dataset bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)': $730,511,989.36 over 6,773 beneficiaries = $107,856.49 a beneficiary. The 2024 annual figure was $109,818 (drug_demand, 5,839 beneficiaries); 2025 is used because it exists

new_note: Net is 94.34% of list: 0.107856 x (1 - 0.056604) = 0.101751 mm USD. Direction checked: share off list. Case against: ASP leaves out 340B and Medicaid prices, which would push net lower
new_source: Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of average sales price, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so the manufacturer's price is the CMS Part B figure divided by 1.06, 5.66% below it: 1 - 1/1.06 = 0.056604. backend/gross_to_net.py holds the 0.5 convention to Part D and derives the Part B deduction from the statute

new_note: Treated to progression, so the PFS route, as atirmociclib converts its median. The 0.6 first written took 1 - exp(-12/13.1), which reads the median as a mean and overstates stopping. SGNDV-001 has not read out, so the closest Phase 3 is RemeGen's same-design Chinese trial, with toripalimab rather than pembrolizumab. Case for higher: real-world EV+P in the US ran a median time to next therapy of 11 months (Ozay et al., ASCO GU 2026, Flatiron Health), which gives 0.5305, and time on treatment usually falls short of PFS
new_source: RC48-C016 (Sheng et al., N Engl J Med 2025;393(23):2324, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2511648, PMID 41124210): median PFS 13.1 months with DV plus toripalimab against 6.5 with chemotherapy, 484 patients with untreated HER2-expressing la/mUC. Constant hazard from the median: 1 - 0.5^(12/13.1) = 0.4700 a year

new_note: JUDGEMENT on the HER2 share: the bottom of the trial sponsor's own range; its midpoint, 70%, gives 0.0961. The base is first-line-treated patients, the same denominator as the Flatiron share in penetration_peak_pct, so the two multiply on one basis. Case against, lower: SGNDV-001 enrols only patients eligible for platinum chemotherapy, so a label that follows the trial would leave out platinum-ineligible patients. Case against, higher: the JMCP flow model predates EV+P, which may have raised the share of la/mUC patients who get first-line therapy. Upper-tract tumours sit in neither the 84,530 nor, necessarily, the 11,600
new_source: Two filters. (1) About 22,542 US patients a year are diagnosed with or progress to la/mUC, of whom 11,600 receive first-line therapy (Hepp et al., 'Epidemiology and treatment patterns for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma: a systematic literature review and gap analysis', J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2021;27(2):240, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2020.20285, PMID 33355035); the figure the vepugratinib seed carries. (2) HER2 IHC 1+ or higher, the SGNDV-001 entry criterion: 'In UC, approximately 60% to 80% of patients have tumors that demonstrate HER2 expression' (Powles et al., SGNDV-001 design paper, Future Oncol 2025;21(21):2705, doi:10.1080/14796694.2025.2535280, PMID 40728126), taken at 60%. 11,600 x 0.60 = 6,960 a year, over the book's 84,530 = 0.08234

new_note: JUDGEMENT: half of what the incumbent measurably captured in its first full year. The eligible pool is first-line-treated patients, the same denominator as this share. SGNDV-001 compares against chemotherapy, not EV+P, and EV+P is already standard in HER2-expressing patients, so DV must take share from Pfizer's own Padcev. Case for lower: no head-to-head against EV+P; nivolumab plus gemcitabine-cisplatin, the other new first-line regimen, reached only 4 of 935 first-line starts (0.4%) from April 2023 to September 2024 (Sonpavde et al., J Clin Oncol 2025;43(16 suppl):e16556, Flatiron); Pfizer's $1.6bn 2025 impairment on updated long-range forecasts. Case for higher: RC48-C016 matched EV-302's OS (31.5 months both) with a PFS hazard ratio of 0.36 against 0.45, and EV+P reached 62% of first-line starts in 2025 in the Ozay series. Check: 0.255 x 84,530 x 0.082338 = 1,775 starts a year, a plateau of about 3,780 US patients at 47% stopping
new_source: Incumbent: enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (Padcev plus Keytruda). Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

(2) A six-cycle course nets $110,435: 2025 Part B spend per claim of $19,510.12 x 6 = $117,061, divided by 1.06. One claim is one dose: in 2024, 1,616,227 mg over 10,844 claims = 149 mg, one 1.8 mg/kg dose. That gives 7,513 course-equivalents. (3) First-line share: Medicare claims were 3,924 in 2022, before the April 2023 first-line label, and 13,091 in 2025. If relapsed use held flat, first line is 70.0%, a lower bound. That gives 5,261 first-line starts. (4) Polivy is a course (d=1), so starts equal the stock. The pool is each year's eligible diagnoses, 19,046 x 0.62 = 11,809. Capture was 44.6% in 2025, Polivy's second full year, and on the fitted curve below (87.3% of peak at index 1) the peak is 51.1%. JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 0.25 gives 12.8%. For: a CD20xCD3 bispecific in place of rituximab, EU approval, and r/r FL response rates near 80%. Against: US entry around 2030 behind Pola-R-CHP, with Roche (glofitamab plus Pola-R-CHP) and AbbVie/Genmab (epcoritamab plus R-CHOP) running their own first-line CD20xCD3 Phase 3s. Net per patient: CMS Part B 2024, J7214, $76,700,767.87 over 154 beneficiaries = $498,056.93, / 1.06 = $469,865, at ECB annual averages of 1.08127 (2023), 1.08238 (2024) and 1.12998 (2025) = EUR 434,550, 434,103 and 415,816 (the 2024 price is used for 2023, whose $220,283 is a part year). Pool: the US severe and moderate haemophilia A patients prophylaxis is given to, 8,011 + 3,319 = 11,330 in federally funded treatment centres over 2012 to 2018 (Soucie JM et al., Haemophilia 2020, PMC8117262, Table 2). Shares 3.1%, 12.5% and 20.8%. Fitted through the engine's identity at 1.55% discontinuation (curve on the midpoint row): a peak of 0.096939 of the unswitched pool a year. For more: superiority on fAAT against weekly pdAAT, every three weeks instead of weekly, recombinant supply free of plasma, and the first new AAT product since 1987. Year 2: stock 28,431 less 10,853 carried = 17,578 starts over 2,242,645 = 0.784%, and the stock is 1.38% of the pool. Multiple 1.0, a judgement. The newest IL-13 is tracking Adbry and not beating it: Ebglyss held 1.84% of Dupixent's beneficiaries in its first full year (3,052 of 165,562) against Adbry's 1.99% in its own (851 of 42,791). The value is half the single-molecule band midpoint amlitelimab carries, which is the low setting a late entrant needs. Crowding: pool_crowding.solve on the three claimants gives no rationed year. At a constant hazard 1 - 0.5^(12/25.5) = 27.83% open a gap each year, and 42.1% of those do not come back: 0.2783 x 0.421 = 11.72% stop a year. Ibrance (palbociclib), CMS Part D 2025, from the quarterly companion 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)': $2,618,976,627.82 over 20,018 beneficiaries = $130,831.08 a beneficiary. Ibrance is the right anchor because it matches on disease, class, partner and care setting: it is Pfizer's own CDK4/6 inhibitor, given with letrozole in first-line metastatic disease and bought under Part D. It was 70.2% of 11,557 first-line CDK4/6i+AI starts (Brufsky et al., Oncologist 2026, doi:10.1093/oncolo/oyag182). It has no adjuvant label, so its per-beneficiary figure is metastatic persistence (8.24 fills a beneficiary). Alternatives from the same file: Kisqali $101,190.62 (17,371) and Verzenio $101,458.11 (14,851). Both are diluted by adjuvant use and by fast growth (6.67 and 6.54 fills). Price per fill is within 5% across the class ($15,175 to $15,881), so the comparator choice is about persistence, not price. Cross-check: 0.5 x $130,831 = $65,416, which is 68% of Ibrance's 2027 Maximum Fair Price annualised ($7,871 per 30 days x 365/30 = $95,764, negotiated_prices). That sits inside the 65% to 167% spread gross_to_net.py measured, and leans conservative.

new_source: ANCHOR, the capture_anchor identity applied to Kisqali, the last CDK4/6 inhibitor to take first-line share, over its metastatic-only window. US revenue from Novartis 20-F inline XBRL (0001370368-24-000004, 0001370368-25-000004): 2021 $339mm, 2022 $472mm, 2023 $1,032mm, 2024 $1,678mm. Net per patient = 0.5 x CMS Part D per beneficiary (drug_demand: $83,131, $78,910, $81,614, $88,305). That gives a stock of 8,156, 11,963, 25,290 and 38,005. Stopping 36.52% a year, from ribociclib+AI real-world treatment duration of 18.3 months (Brufsky et al.): 0.5^(12/18.3) = 63.48% remain. New starts: 2022 = 11,963 - 8,156 x 0.6348 = 6,786; 2023 = 25,290 - 11,963 x 0.6348 = 17,696; 2024 = 38,005 - 25,290 x 0.6348 = 21,952. The pool is the annual endocrine-based first-line cohort, which is Kisqali's first-line label: 65,000 x 0.843 = 54,795. Capture: 12.4%, 32.3%, 40.1%. 2024 includes adjuvant starts from the September 2024 NATALEE approval, so 2023 is the clean year: 32.3%. CROSS-CHECK: the revenue basis counts 5.57 Kisqali patients per Part D beneficiary in 2023, against 2.07 for Ibrance in 2025 (41,428 / 20,018). Restated at Ibrance's ratio (stock 9,402 and 4,363), the 2023 capture is 12.1%. The convention probably fits Kisqali's net price or payer mix badly, and the revenue anchor overstates by up to 2.7x. MULTIPLE 0.4, A JUDGEMENT: 0.4 x 32.3% = 12.9%, which also sits at the beneficiary-basis capture. The case for more: FOURLIGHT-3 is the only CDK trial designed for superiority over CDK4/6 inhibitors, CDK4 selectivity spares neutropenia, and Pfizer held 70% of first-line starts. The case against: this is the fourth CDK agent into a crowded class; palbociclib is generic from 2027 (US basic patent RE47739, 2027-03-05 plus paediatric exclusivity to 2027-09-05), so payers will step through a generic; ribociclib has first-line overall survival data this drug will not have at launch; and oral SERDs (camizestrant) are moving into first line. The whole value rests on that result.

new_note: two things to argue with. First, evERA's own enrolled population was 55.5% ESR1-mutated (207 of 373; N Engl J Med 2026;395(13):1285-1298), well above the figure taken here, which is the case for a larger layer; a trial that tests circulating tumour DNA in every screened patient will find more mutations than routine practice does, which is why the real-world figure was taken instead. Second, and biasing this high, no further narrowing for line of therapy is applied: the 160,000 is the whole prevalent metastatic HR-positive HER2-negative stock, while the eligible patient has already progressed on a CDK4/6 inhibitor. At steady state nearly all of this pool passes through that point, but not all of it is there at once

new_source: a judgement.
